evidence.note: Documentation states that newly created OAuth clients start in a pending state and must be reviewed and accepted by a Cal.com admin.

steps.title: Choose the App Integration Model
steps.detail: Decide between configuring standard OAuth 2.0 clients (supporting confidential clients with a client_secret or public clients using PKCE) or platform/managed-user workflows where backend-managed users are created programmatically.
steps.notes: Determines how users and authentication tokens will be managed.

steps.title: Create an OAuth Client
steps.detail: Navigate to the Cal.com developer dashboard at https://app.cal.com/settings/developer/oauth to register a new OAuth client, providing app details and at least one scope.
steps.notes: Requires human login to the developer portal.

probes.summary: No OpenID Connect discovery document at 1 candidate location(s).
RFC 8414 authorization server metadata found (issuer: https://cal.com).
Authorization endpoint (from discovery metadata) responds to a request with a fake client_id (HTTP 200).
Token endpoint (from discovery metadata) is live: an unauthenticated request with a fake code returned OAuth error "invalid_request" (HTTP 400).
Discovery metadata does not advertise a registration_endpoint, so dynamic client registration is likely unsupported.
Link loads (HTTP 200) — redirects to sign-in, as expected for a developer console.

limitations: No accounts were created, no forms submitted, no OAuth apps registered, and no credentials were used. Probes are unauthenticated GET requests against public discovery documents, endpoints and documentation pages, plus one unauthenticated POST to the token endpoint with a fake authorization code and a nonexistent client_id (to confirm it answers with an OAuth error).
Review timelines are only marked as sourced when an official provider page states them. Community-reported timelines are labeled as such.
